title: Running Median Latency
summary: Report the median request latency after every sample in a high-volume stream.

stages.title: Streaming median
stages.requirement:
Implement `MedianTracker` with `add(latency_ms)` and `median()`. `median()` returns the
median of every value added so far, as a float: the middle value for an odd count, the
mean of the two middle values for an even count. It returns `None` before any value is added.

```python
t = MedianTracker()
t.add(5); t.median()   # -> 5.0
t.add(15); t.median()  # -> 10.0
t.add(1); t.median()   # -> 5.0
```

Tests call `add` and `median` 100,000 times each, so sorting on every call is too slow.

visibleTests.name: test_example
visibleTests.code:
def test_example():
    t = MedianTracker()
    t.add(5)
    assert t.median() == 5.0
    t.add(15)
    assert t.median() == 10.0
    t.add(1)
    assert t.median() == 5.0

    assert MedianTracker().median() is None

def test_returns_float():
    t = MedianTracker()
    t.add(1)
    t.add(2)
    assert t.median() == 1.5 and isinstance(t.median(), float)

hiddenTests.name: test_matches_sorted_oracle
hiddenTests.code:
def test_matches_sorted_oracle():
    import random
    rng = random.Random(3)
    t = MedianTracker()
    seen = []
    for _ in range(2000):
        v = rng.randint(-1000, 1000)
        t.add(v)
        seen.append(v)
        s = sorted(seen)
        n = len(s)
        expected = float(s[n // 2]) if n % 2 else (s[n // 2 - 1] + s[n // 2]) / 2
        assert t.median() == expected

hiddenTests.name: test_large_stream

hints: Split the values into a lower half and an upper half. The median sits at their boundary.
Use a max-heap for the lower half (store negated values with `heapq`) and a min-heap for the upper half.
After each add, rebalance so the lower heap has the same number of items as the upper heap, or one more. The median is then a heap top, or the mean of both tops.

solution.explanation:
Two heaps partition the data: `low` (a max-heap) holds the smaller half and `high` (a
min-heap) the larger. The invariant `len(low) - len(high)` in {0, 1} puts the median at
`low`'s top (odd count) or at the mean of both tops (even count). Each add is
O(log n) with at most one rebalancing move, and each median query is O(1).
